text:
Yes. A 20,000 mAh power bank is allowed on a US flight, but only in your carry-on, never in checked bags.

**Why it's allowed**
- Watt-hours are mAh × 3.7 ÷ 1,000, so 20,000 mAh is about 74 Wh. The FAA limit for a spare lithium-ion battery or power bank is 100 Wh, so you're well under it. ([FAA: Airline Passengers and Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries))
- Under 100 Wh, the FAA sets no quantity limit for personal use. ([FAA PackSafe: Lithium Batteries](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- If the printed rating is in Wh, use that number. Check the label on the unit.

**Rules to follow**
- Keep it in your carry-on. If a carry-on gets gate-checked, take the power bank out and keep it with you in the cabin. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- Protect the terminals from short circuits. Use the original packaging, tape over the ports, or a pouch or case. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- Don't bring a damaged or recalled power bank. ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7))
- If it gets hot, swells, or smokes, tell the crew right away. ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/))

**Airlines can be stricter than the FAA**
The FAA says many airlines limit how many power banks you can carry, so check yours before you fly ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)). A retailer's roundup (Dealectric, October 2026) reports these US policies:
- Southwest: one power bank per customer, and you can't charge it from seat power.
- American and Delta: two per passenger, with no recharging on board.
- JetBlue: two per customer, not charged from seat power.

I haven't verified those against the airlines' own pages, so confirm with your carrier. The same roundup says many airlines, especially outside the US, now restrict using a power bank in flight. If you're flying internationally, check that airline's rules too. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/best-power-banks-for-flying))

If you tell me your airline, I can help narrow down what applies to you.
